results.description: `.gitignore` at the workspace root must contain a `target/` entry to exclude build artifacts.
The branch checked out at the workspace root must match the configured dev_branch (default: dev).

violations.llm_prompt:
WHAT: The branch checked out at the workspace root must match the configured
dev_branch (`[config] dev_branch`, default `"dev"`).

WHY: Committing local work directly on `main`, a stale feature branch, or
whatever branch happened to be checked out makes history hard to follow and
risks pushing unreviewed work to a protected branch by accident. Enforcing a
single, predictable local-development branch keeps that discipline explicit
rather than tribal knowledge.

BEFORE (violating):
  $ git branch --show-current
  main                # local work committed directly on main  ❌

AFTER (compliant):
  $ git branch --show-current
  dev                 # matches the configured dev_branch  ✅

EDGE CASES:
- Skipped entirely when the `CI` environment variable is set -- CI legitimately
  checks out other pipeline branches (test, main, int, uat) to audit them, and
  this rule targets local development only.
- A project using a different trunk-adjacent branch name (e.g. "develop") can
  override the default via `[config] dev_branch = "develop"`.
- Detached HEAD or a directory outside any git repository cannot be evaluated
  and passes rather than failing spuriously.

results.description: The project root must not contain both a build.* script and a bootstrap.*.
Library crates should have an examples/ directory demonstrating canonical.
Exactly one architecture.toml may exist — either at the project root or.
Every file and directory at the project root must appear in the configured.

violations.message: Unexpected entry 'LICENSE-APACHE' at project level (not in project whitelist)
violations.expected: Only entries from the project whitelist
violations.fix_hint: Remove 'LICENSE-APACHE' if it doesn't belong at the project root, or add it to [[policy.project]] in architecture.policy.toml if it's an intentional entry
violations.llm_prompt:
WHAT: Every file and directory at the project root must appear in the configured
whitelist — unlisted entries are a violation.

WHY: An unconstrained root accumulates stray config files, IDE folders, and
temporary artifacts over time, burying the actual project structure and making
the top-level layout undiscoverable. The whitelist is a forcing function for
intentional placement.

BEFORE (violating):
  /
    .myeditor/        ❌ — not in whitelist
    temp_output/      ❌ — not in whitelist
    Cargo.toml

AFTER (compliant):
  /
    Cargo.toml        ✅
    bootstrap.sh      ✅
    docs/             ✅

EDGE CASES:
- To legitimately add a new root entry, first add it to [[policy.project]]'s
  entries list in policy/rules/policy.toml, then create the file/directory.
- Hidden files starting with `.` that are needed (e.g. .gitignore, .github/)
  should be in the whitelist; do not suppress the rule to avoid adding them.
